lines: Here's the whole psalm in one bite, friend: there's NOWHERE David can go that God isn't already there, and NOTHING about him God doesn't already know, not his steps, not his naps, not his words before he says them (Ps 139:1-12).
Heavens, Sheol, the farthest sea, pitch dark. Every hiding spot gets the same answer: "You are there" (Ps 139:8). I lose my apron in my OWN kitchen, and David can't find ONE spot God isn't.
And God doesn't just know David, He MADE him. He knit him together in his mother's womb and wrote all his days in His book before one of them came to be (Ps 139:13-16).
I think being known that well could feel scary. David calls it "too wonderful for me" (Ps 139:6), and he says, "How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God" (Ps 139:17).
Then he gets fiery about God's enemies, the ones who take God's name in vain, and says, "I count them as my enemies" (Ps 139:20-22).

But he doesn't end pointing at them. He ends pointing at HIMSELF: "Search me, O God, and know my heart" (Ps 139:23). Friend, I used to hide my crooked cookies at the back of the tray. David slides the WHOLE tray across the counter.
So the God who searched David at the start (Ps 139:1) is the God David invites in at the end, asking Him to "lead me in the way everlasting" (Ps 139:24).
